title: The Deadly London Acid Fog: When Air Turned to Poison

phenomenon.type: Toxic Radiation Fog & Severe Thermal Inversion
phenomenon.meteorological_trigger: High-pressure anticyclone settled over southern England, trapping cold moist surface air beneath a warm ceiling at 100-200 meters altitude.
phenomenon.chemical_mechanism: Fog water droplets acted as micro-reactors. Sulfur dioxide (SO2) catalyzed with atmospheric nitrogen dioxide (NO2) and soot particles, rapidly oxidizing into dilute sulfuric acid (H2SO4) mist.

impact.visibility: Reduced to a few inches ('could not see your feet')
impact.indoor_penetration: Cinema and theater screenings canceled as smoke blocked projector beams indoors
impact.livestock: Prize cattle choked and died of respiratory failure at the Smithfield Agricultural Show
impact.transport: Ambulances grounded; walking inspectors used flares to guide double-decker buses

fatalities.primary_causes: Acute bronchitis, bronchopneumonia, respiratory and cardiac arrest

forensic_smoking_gun.finding: Direct hour-by-hour lockstep correlation between SO2 / smoke concentration peaks and sudden quadrupling of daily mortalities.

historical_resolution: The disaster ended the era of unregulated domestic coal burning, leading directly to the landmark UK Clean Air Act of 1956.
